newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares soar on foreign demand, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares soar on foreign demand, seen up.

text.p: Leading Russian shares soared on Friday to a new record on strong foreign demand and healthy volumes and traders forecast a further rise next week.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares jumped to 262.52, breaking Monday's record 360.72. Total market turnover was a strong $68.8 million.

"I think market growth will continue next week, especially in the shares which have lagged behind," said Alfa-Capital director of sales Alexander Bubnovsky, who said he saw active Western buying during the day.
He said metals mining concern Norilsk Nickel and second-tier shares in particular would see overdue growth next week.

Traders said Norilsk NKEL.RTS, which surged about 12 percent to $7.14 from $6.35 at Thursday's close, rose on expectations of its issue of ADRs, share look-alikes which allow stock to be traded on foreign markets.
The company said on Friday it still planned an ADR issue by July.
"I can see Norilsk Nickel at $8.50 and if it issues ADRs at $10-$11," CentreInvest Securities chief trader Alexander Babayan said.
Babayan said Kubanelectrosvayz on the Russian Trading System second tier was also rising ahead of an expected ADR issue.
"Everyone is waiting for Kubanelectrosvyaz ADRs," he said.

Trinfiko trader Grigory Pinsky said demand was also strong for international long-distance telecom Rostelekom RTKM.RTS, which rose to $4.05 from $3.85. National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3200 from $0.3056.
Babayan said recent government decisions to restructure monopolies were also helping to boost the market.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Friday a regulation giving equal access to natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom GAZP.RTS would be ready within a month.
"The market was quite strong today," said Bubnovsky."We are very optimistic."
